model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: TTM non-cash stock-based compensation: FY2025 10-K cash flow 38.733 less 9M-2025 32.415 plus 9M-2026 36.080 (Q3-2026 10-Q FFO reconciliation and cash flow statement)
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at the latest count: 528.82m common shares outstanding (10-Q cover, 27 Oct 2026; same as 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet) + 3.25m OP units + 0.53m restricted stock + 1.2m treasury-method dilution from 9.1m unsettled forward-sale shares (Q3-2026 EPS note). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flow, and external growth funded by new ATM equity is assumed value-neutral and excluded from the growth path.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC: the capitalised flow (AFFO) is already after interest. USD basis: ~4.3% 10-year US Treasury assumption + ~0.8 beta x 5% ERP = ~8.0-8.5%; base 8.0%, bull 7.5%, bear 9.0%. The risk-free input is an assumption, not a fetched quote.
inputs.lease_treatment: Ground-lease cost is already inside property operating expenses and therefore inside Normalized FFO; no separate lease path and no lease liability deducted.
inputs.nci_treatment: Normalized FFO is stated attributable to common stockholders (NCI share of depreciation and normalising items already removed). OP units (3.25m) are counted in the share base rather than as a deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine with net debt held at zero. Reason: Ventas is a healthcare REIT (SHOP senior housing, outpatient medical & research, triple-net); FFO/AFFO is post-interest, so capitalising it at a WACC or deducting the $12.4bn of debt afterwards would count the debt twice. Reported debt and cash are recorded as reported_total_debt / reported_cash for audit only. AFFO IS DERIVED, NOT DISCLOSED: Ventas reports only Nareit FFO and Normalized FFO. Base AFFO = Q3-2026 Normalized FFO 514.227 x 4 = 2,056.9 (NEW definition, which from Q1-2026 adds back non-cash SBC) less TTM SBC 42.4 (re-deducted, so the definition change is neutralised) less maintenance capex 450 (9M-2026 'Other capital expenditures' 319.3 annualised to 426 and rounded up for Q4 seasonality; treated as 100% recurring because the 10-Q does not split FAD capex -- conservative) less straight-line rent ~34 (9M 25.4 annualised) = ~1,531, or ~$2.87 per fully diluted share. Redevelopment/development spend (214.3 in 9M-2026) is growth capex and is not deducted; the growth path is correspondingly limited to same-store/organic growth. ENGINE MAPPING: base_revenue = Q3-2026 revenue 1,831.8 x 4; ebitda_margin_path = pre-SBC AFFO margin (21.47%); sbc_pct_path = SBC % of revenue; D&A, capex, tax and working capital are zero because they are already inside AFFO. growth_rates are AFFO-per-existing-share growth, NOT reported revenue growth: reported revenue will grow faster through acquisitions funded by new equity, which this model treats as value-neutral. Normalized FFO figures for 2025 and earlier in the Metrics CSV are on the OLD (post-SBC) basis and are not comparable with 2026 quarters without adding SBC back. No FY2026 guidance paragraph is carried in the 10-Q text (guidance is in the 8-K earnings release, not in Extracted/), so year-1 growth is judged from the Q3-2026 same-store prints, not from guidance. Entry-price hurdle of 15% is the house hurdle and is very demanding for a REIT; read the entry price as a deep-value marker.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: normalized_ffo_per_share_3yr_cagr (FY2022 $2.99 -> FY2025 $3.48 on diluted shares, old post-SBC definition both ends)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (7.2% 3yr) and revenue CAGR (12.2% 3yr) are driven by share issuance (shares 403m -> 463m FY2022-FY2025, 529m by Sep-2026), not per-share compounding; GAAP EPS is depreciation-dominated and swings through zero, so no EPS CAGR is given. Normalized FFO per share (5.2% 3yr; 4.7% over the four years from FY2021) is the meaningful series. FFO history in the CSV starts FY2021, so no 5-year figure.
historical_growth.notes: fcf_* here is Normalized FFO per diluted share, the closest disclosed proxy for owner cash flow. Recent pace is faster: 9M-2026 Normalized FFO per diluted share $2.90 vs $2.65 restated 9M-2025, +9.4%.

base.narrative: SHOP same-store NOI growth fades from ~15% as occupancy (92.1% same-store) approaches its ceiling; OM&R grows 2-3%; NNN flat.

bull.narrative: Senior-housing supply stays scarce through the 80+ demographic wave; pricing power replaces occupancy as the growth lever and accretive acquisitions add per-share growth.

bear.narrative: Occupancy plateaus near 90%, labour costs absorb rate increases, new supply returns, and maintenance capex runs heavier on an ageing SHOP estate.

scenario_narratives.base: AFFO per existing share grows 10% next year and fades to 3.5% by year 9. The driver is SHOP, now roughly 59% of NOI, where same-store NOI has grown 15-16% for eight straight quarters on occupancy gains (same-store 87.0% -> 92.1% in two years) and RevPOR up ~7%. Occupancy cannot compound much beyond the low 90s, so the path steps down each year toward rent-growth-only. OM&R contributes 2-3%; NNN is flat after the Q3-2026 same-store decline of 5.2%. Capitalised at an 8.0% cost of equity with 3.0% terminal growth.
scenario_narratives.bull: The demographic tailwind and a decade of under-building keep SHOP NOI compounding at double digits for three more years, with rate rather than occupancy doing the work, and the cost of equity settles at 7.5% as the market keeps paying a premium for the growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: SHOP growth halves as occupancy tops out and wage inflation returns; NNN lease resets continue to cut rent; maintenance capex takes a larger share of NOI. The market re-rates healthcare REITs to a 9% cost of equity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25. The bull case is already what the share price assumes (about 31x derived AFFO), and the bear case is an ordinary cyclical normalisation of senior housing rather than a solvency event, so neither tail earns extra weight.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Ventas is valued on the cash an owner could actually take out: Normalized FFO less stock compensation, maintenance capex and straight-line rent, capitalised at the cost of equity. Debt is not deducted because the flow is already after interest. Only organic, same-store growth is credited to the existing share; acquisitions funded by new equity are assumed to earn their cost of capital.
key_risks_to_valuation: AFFO is derived, not disclosed: all 'other capital expenditures' (~$450m/yr) are treated as maintenance. If true FAD capex is nearer $350m, AFFO per share is ~6% higher and value rises proportionately.

External growth is excluded. Ventas issued 47m shares in nine months at ~$87 to fund acquisitions; if those are accretive per share (issuing at an implied ~4.5% FFO yield to buy at 7%+ yields), the model understates growth.
Terminal value is most of the result and moves ~15% for each 0.5pt of cost of equity; a healthcare REIT trading at ~31x AFFO is a long-duration asset.
SHOP is an operating business with labour-cost and occupancy risk, unlike triple-net rent; the 2020-2022 experience (Normalized FFO/share ~$2.90-2.99) shows the downside.
The 10-year Treasury yield behind the cost of equity is an assumption (~4.3%), not a fetched quote.
$12.4bn of debt at fixed rates below current market reprices upward as it matures, a drag on FFO growth not separately modelled.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 73.82-101.60
data_sources.financials: VTR 10-Q Q3-2026 (FFO reconciliation, cash flow statement, EPS note, balance sheet, cover share count), 10-K FY2025, VTR_Metrics.csv and kpis table (FFO, FFONormalized, NOI, same-store KPIs)
data_sources.qualitative: Q3-2026 10-Q MD&A (segment NOI, same-store growth, ATM forward sales, liquidity). No Analysis JSON existed at build time.
